commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[shellbox] Add persistent container tasks and host capabilities

Add persistent Shellbox tasks with a primary container and supporting runtime containers. The local factory starts each member in bubblewrap; members share private loopback and retain separate filesystems and PID namespaces. Single machines use the same task representation. Timeout, cancellation, member failure and TTL reclaim the task.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    driver[Trusted driver and provider credentials]
    relay[Bounded HTTP request/response relay]
    process[Shared ProcessSession lifecycle]
    pipe[Local and Docker binary pipes]
    sdk[Daytona text transport and shared codec]
    driver <--> relay
    relay <--> process
    process <--> pipe
    process <--> sdk
    subgraph task[Bubblewrap task: denied external networking]
        primary[Primary container and HTTP helper]
        runtime[Runtime container]
        primary <-->|Private loopback| runtime
    end
    pipe <--> primary
```

`StreamProcessSession` shares read/write serialization, bounded stderr and cancellation-safe closure across pipe and SDK adapters. Adapters supply transport operations; Daytona's host and guest bridge share the text frame codec. The HTTP relay carries complete bounded requests and responses over that byte stream. Pydantic handles host-side message validation and JSON/base64 encoding; the guest helper uses only the standard library. Provider authentication stays with the trusted driver. Local, Docker, gVisor and Daytona support process sessions; QEMU, ShellSim and the existing Iris backend retain their command/file-transfer interfaces.

Local machines support prepared OCI images and persistent BusyBox/bubblewrap namespaces. A delegated cgroup v2 parent enforces CPU and RAM limits across each machine's descendants. Declared limits require delegation or an explicit ignore policy. Digest-pinned OCI layouts can be verified and reused offline. Disk quotas and accelerator allocation remain unsupported; local execution shares the worker's kernel and requires an isolated worker.

Harbor integration #10628 builds on this contract to import Compose tasks. Native Iris container groups and driver-to-task endpoint authorization are deferred to standalone draft #10822; this change requires no Iris controller rollout and preserves the existing Iris backend.

Part of #10486 and #10489.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
Preserve BF16 checkpoint payloads in TensorStore writes (#10792)

Let TensorStore copy staged checkpoint arrays when issuing writes. With
referenced-source writes, a 2.5 MiB BF16 array of shape `(5, 64, 64,
64)` filled with 0.125 restores entirely as zeros: all 1,310,720
elements differ. Copying preserves every value. A standalone file-backed
zarr3 reproducer confirms the failure with TensorStore 0.1.84; the
underlying cause remains unresolved.

Copying is enabled for every dtype, adding host-copy work and transient
memory beyond the staged-array budget. The existing staging and commit
lifecycle is unchanged.

The affected CPU suite passed 1,348 tests with seven skipped. Its five
checkpoint-path failures also reproduce on unchanged main.
